Enhancing heating performance in electric vehicles via integrated cabin waste heat recovery: from co-simulation to real-vehicle validation
Limitations of the factorized incidence angle modifier: Comparison with experimental efficiency data in a Fresnel solar plant
abstract: Accurate modeling of solar Fresnel plants is essential for reliable energy and economic evaluations. Optical efficiency is usually estimated using factorized incidence angle modifier (IAM) curves provided by manufacturers, but this simplification introduces significant errors at high incidence angles. This study compared theoretical efficiency derived from IAM data with experimental measurements collected in a Fresnel plant monitored over several years. Cosine losses affected by factorization and end losses associated with the actual receiver length were analyzed and corrected. The original IAM underestimated efficiency in winter, and the applied corrections reduced these seasonal deviations. However, the corrected curves overestimated efficiency by 30% to 40% during all months due to additional losses not included in the IAM, like tracking errors. The application of the corrected IAM increased annual energy prediction only by 2.6%, since the largest variation, 11%, occurred during winter months, which contribute less to the total value. These results show that IAM corrections improve the seasonal consistency of efficiency estimates and the accurate representation of curves, but significant deviations persist under actual operating conditions, and corrections don’t reduce annual energy production errors. Experimental validation over the entire year and enhanced modeling are required for reliable performance predictions in Fresnel installations.

title: Grid impact of replacing residential gas boiler with heat pump water heaters in South Korea
Experimental thermal and desalination performance analysis of a spectral beam-splitting PV/T-driven membrane distillation system
Wind- and solar-powered green ammonia for China’s low-carbon energy transition: High-resolution assessment and cost-optimal siting under land-use constraints
Self-regulated compression and expansion effect on spray and mixing of a vibration gasoline combustor under ignition fluctuation
Dynamic modelling and control of a nuclear hybrid energy system with high-temperature electrolysis for electricity and hydrogen production
abstract: Nuclear power represents a promising enabler for low-carbon, large-scale hydrogen production, as it can provide continuous, dispatchable thermal and electrical energy. In particular, the availability of thermal power enables the integration of nuclear reactors with High-Temperature Steam Electrolysis (HTSE) systems in so-called Nuclear Hybrid Energy Systems (NHES), where the reactor thermal power can be flexibly allocated either to electricity or hydrogen production. This work presents a Modelica-based simulation framework for an illustrative NHES configuration, explicitly resolving the dynamic coupling between the HTSE plant, the intermediate heat transfer loop, and the nuclear steam cycle. This system-level representation enables the derivation of operational maps and indicative flexibility limits arising from the coupled nuclear–hydrogen dynamics, beyond what can be captured by component-level transient analyses. A one-dimensional representation of the electrolyser is proposed to capture the dynamics of key thermal stress indicators, such as temperature gradients, which define the operational constraints. In the proposed configuration, the entire reactor power is directed to hydrogen production, with approximately 7% supplied directly as thermal energy to the HTSE plant and the remainder converted to electrical power through the steam cycle, resulting in a hydrogen production rate of 107.7 t/d. The NHES simulator is applied to investigate the versatile output allocation capabilities of the overall architecture. Two operational strategies are compared, prioritising either electricity or hydrogen output. Results show that significant flexibility can be achieved with minimal perturbations on the nuclear reactor, which operates continuously at rated conditions. However, it is observed that rapid variations in hydrogen production rates can impose severe thermal transients on the electrolyser, in particular for excursions exceeding 10% of the nominal value, for which temperature variation rates may exceed the commonly accepted limit of 3°C/min. The analysis demonstrates that the flexibility of the proposed NHES architecture can provide significant support in the context of the energy transition, contributing to preserving grid stability and, at the same time, scaling up the supply of low-carbon hydrogen.

title: Physics-informed modular modeling of a gas turbine with component-level thermodynamic constraints and system-level consistency
abstract: Accurate and physically consistent modeling of gas turbine systems is essential for improving performance prediction, reliability, and energy efficiency. Conventional data-driven approaches often lack physical interpretability, while purely physics-based models struggle to capture complex nonlinear system behavior. This study presents a modular physics-informed modeling framework for gas turbine performance and emission prediction, in which thermodynamic constraints are embedded at the component level and preserved during system-level integration. The proposed approach incorporates differential thermodynamic relations for compressor and turbine components, along with an energy balance formulation for the combustor, directly into the learning process. A coordinated system-level fine-tuning strategy is introduced to enforce consistency across interconnected components and mitigate the accumulation of integration errors. The framework is evaluated using three datasets with varying levels of complexity, including a high-fidelity simulated turbofan engine dataset based on Pratt & Whitney PW-4056, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) benchmark dataset, and a real industrial gas turbine Predictive Emission Monitoring System (PEMS) dataset for emission prediction. At the component level, the physics-informed formulation achieves mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) below 0.28% for key variables, outperforming conventional neural network models. At the system level, the proposed integration strategy reduces prediction errors by up to 86.39% for thrust, 81.85% for thrust-specific fuel consumption, and 75.70% for overall pressure ratio relative to baseline data-driven models. On the C-MAPSS dataset, the approach maintains MAPE values below 0.33% under limited sensor conditions. For the industrial PEMS dataset, the model achieves mean absolute errors of 0.8536 mg/m 3 for Carbon monoxide (CO) and 4.8419 mg/m 3 for Nitrogen oxides (NOx) under real operating conditions. These results demonstrate that integrating thermodynamic constraints with data-driven learning improves prediction accuracy, robustness, and physical consistency, particularly under varying operating conditions across gas turbine systems. The proposed framework provides a foundation for developing physics-consistent digital twins for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance applications.

title: An adaptive purge control strategy with spatial awareness of purge difficulty for hydrogen leakage in proton exchange membrane fuel cell stacks
Large-scale heat pumps: Development of an easy-to-use heating capacity model for diverse configurations and refrigerants
abstract: Large-scale heat pumps are a key technology for decarbonizing industrial and district heating systems, yet no simple, broadly applicable model exists for estimating their heating capacity across diverse configurations and refrigerants for varying operating temperatures and load conditions. This gap motivates the hypothesis that heating capacity can be accurately predicted by separating refrigerant thermodynamic properties, expressed as volumetric heating capacity, from heat pump design parameters, expressed as volumetric flow rate, with only a single nominal operating point required for calibration. To test this hypothesis, a regression-based model is developed, relying on heat source and sink temperatures and compressor frequency as inputs, with regression parameters provided for 48 refrigerants. The modeling approach is first assessed using highly dynamic measurement data from a prototype air/water heat pump tested in a climate chamber. This prototype data also serves to assess the applicability of a previously developed water/water coefficient of performance model to air/water heat pumps and to evaluate the impact of frequency control on the coefficient of performance. For validation, quasi-steady-state performance data from eleven commercial large-scale heat pumps is used, yielding a mean coefficient of determination of 0.94 and a mean absolute percentage error of 4.2 %. These results demonstrate that the model is sufficiently accurate for system design applications such as preliminary design and feasibility studies, despite the necessary simplifications. The model complements previously published coefficient of performance regression functions, providing a complete, easy-to-use framework for modeling quasi-steady-state heat pump operation across a wide range of configurations and refrigerants.

title: Numerical Investigation of a Tuscan Kale-inspired bionic flow field for PEMFCs with optimized inter-branch channels architecture
Uncertainty-aware process design using constrained Bayesian optimization: An application to Fischer–Tropsch mixture separation
Multi-objective optimization and techno-economic evaluation of microwave-assisted pyrolysis of hemp biomass for sustainable biochar and bio-oil production
abstract: As the world seeks sustainable alternatives to fossil-based energy and materials, microwave-assisted pyrolysis has emerged as a promising next-generation thermochemical technology, offering rapid volumetric heating, superior energy efficiency, and precise control over product formation. This study delivers a comprehensive assessment of microwave-assisted pyrolysis applied to hemp biomass, integrating experimental investigation, techno-economic analysis, and multi-objective optimization to evaluate its viability as a carbon-negative biochar and bio-oil production pathway. Experiments across varying microwave power levels revealed that methane dominated the greenhouse gas emission profile, while the optimal 1.0 kW condition achieved a remarkable 88.7% reduction in emission intensity compared to 0.8 kW. Carbon partitioning analysis demonstrated that 62–68% of biomass carbon was retained in the biochar, a testament to the process’s strong carbon-fixation capability. Elemental characterization confirmed progressive carbonization yielding stable, aromatic biochar with favorable atomic ratios for long-term carbon sequestration. Techno-economic analysis identified electricity as the primary cost driver, with biochar revenue forming the economic backbone of the process. Multi-objective optimization via a GA–TOPSIS framework identified 1.0 kW as the optimal operating condition, balancing cost, revenue, and environmental performance. Further improvements through energy recovery and carbon-credit integration could enhance the economic competitiveness of MAP for sustainable biochar production.

title: Physics-informed LLM-guided dynamic spatio-temporal graph deep network for short-term wind farm power forecasting
abstract: Wind energy plays a critical role in meeting global electricity demand and decarbonisation targets, accounting for a substantial and growing share of renewable power generation worldwide. However, the inherently intermittent, non-stationary, and spatially coupled nature of wind severely complicates the reliable integration of wind farms into power systems. In particular, short-term wind power forecasting at ultra-short (10-minute) and short (one-hour) horizons is essential for real-time dispatch, reserve allocation, and grid stability, yet remains challenging due to wake interactions, regime shifts in wind direction and speed, sensor noise in supervisory control and data acquisition, and dynamically evolving turbine-to-turbine dependencies. To address these challenges, a Physics-Informed directionality-aware Large Language Guided Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Deep Model is proposed for short-term wind farm power forecasting. The proposed framework integrates physics-informed power-curve cleaning, dynamic graph construction guided by a large language model, and spatio-temporal graph convolutional networks to explicitly model regime-dependent, directed turbine interactions. Unlike conventional static or correlation-based graphs, the large language model infers context-conditioned adjacency structures that adapt to changing wind regimes while preserving interpretability and reproducibility through schema validation and fallback mechanisms. Extensive experiments are conducted on a large-scale, high-resolution dataset from a multi-turbine wind farm, benchmarking the proposed framework against 14 well-known recurrent deep learning, transformer-based, and hybrid ensemble models with two recent LLM-based forecasting baselines. For 10-minute-ahead forecasting, the proposed model (LLXSTG) substantially outperforms the JST-Transformer, achieving 66.5% and 67.9% reductions in mean absolute error and root mean squared error, respectively, together with a 19.3% improvement in R-value. When compared with the advanced ensemble learning baseline, the proposed model yields 32.6% lower mean absolute error, 26.3% lower root mean squared error, and a 4.1% increase in R-value, demonstrating clear gains even against strong non-transformer architectures. At the one-hour-ahead horizon, the proposed model maintains its superiority under increased forecast uncertainty, reducing average absolute error and root mean squared error by 55.2% and 54.2%, respectively, relative to JST-Transformer, while improving the R-value by 11.5%. Compared with the advanced ensemble, the proposed model achieves 35.0% lower average absolute error, 29.6% lower root mean squared error, and a 4.9% increase in correlation. These consistent improvements across both ultra-short and short-term horizons highlight the effectiveness of integrating causality awareness, large language-guided dynamic graph construction, and spatio-temporal learning for robust wind farm power forecasting.

title: Experimental and computational investigation of water cooling by natural evaporation

Enhancement and mechanistic elucidation of thermal and electrochemical performance for proton exchange membrane fuel cells with wavy integrated cooling configurations under diverse coolant flow conditions
Magnetically redirected cryo-electric harvesting from charged snowflakes: A theoretical framework for energy amid storm mitigation
Thermodynamic modelling and techno-economic assessment of mechanical vapour recompression for decarbonising low-temperature alumina refining
abstract: Industrial process heat is a major source of energy use and emissions in alumina refining. Low-temperature alumina refineries have recoverable heat and vapour streams that can potentially be upgraded to useful steam conditions using mechanical vapour recompression (MVR). This study presents a thermodynamic and techno-economic assessment of open-cycle MVR for low-temperature alumina refining and compares it with direct electric boilers. The model evaluates how waste-heat temperature, required steam temperature and plant capacity affect compression requirements, coefficient of performance (COP), capital expenditure (CAPEX), operating expenditure (OPEX), levelised cost of heat (LCOH) and operational emissions. The results show that temperature lift is the main driver of MVR performance. Feasible MVR cases achieve COP values of approximately 2–7, corresponding to 62–70% of the Carnot limit. Warmer waste-heat sources reduce compression work and can reduce the number of required compression stages. The economic results show that MVR becomes more competitive at larger plant capacities because specific CAPEX decreases and the energy-saving benefit of higher COP becomes more important. Median MVR–DEB cost parity occurs near the MW scale under favourable temperature-lift conditions. The emissions analysis shows that MVR can reduce operational emissions relative to gas-fired steam generation when electricity carbon intensity is sufficiently low. The results identify the source-temperature, steam-temperature and capacity conditions under which MVR can provide a competitive alternative to direct electric steam generation for low-temperature alumina refining.

title: Corrigendum: Utilization of triply periodic minimal surfaces for performance enhancement of adsorption cooling systems: Computational fluid dynamics analysis
Experimentally validated machine learning surrogates for rapid power coefficient prediction of Darrieus hydrokinetic turbines under canal and river flow conditions
Optimal design of integrated power-to-hydrogen and methanol co-production system under renewable energy uncertainty
Impacts of dynamic behaviours of thermal energy storage on dispatch optimization for combined heat and power plants
abstract: Thermal Energy Storage (TES) systems play an important role in improving flexibility in Combined Heat and Power (CHP) plants by decoupling heat production from demand requirements. Previous studies on dispatch optimization normally consider constraints based on static TES limits, assuming constant charging and discharging capabilities regardless of the state of charge (SOC). This approach ignores the influence of SOC on actual TES limits, i.e., feasible charging and discharging rates, which can lead to infeasible dispatch. To solve this problem, this work integrates dynamic TES modelling into CHP dispatch optimization through a two-stage approach that enforces dynamic TES constraints and identifies when constraint violations occur. Using a real CHP plant as a case study with electricity market data, the SOC-dependent dynamic formulation is benchmarked against conventional static-constraint approaches. Results show that static constraint assumptions lead to infeasible dispatch for 53 hours across 49 days annually when only the day-ahead market participation is considered. Such infeasible planning can be affected by multi-market participation, price volatility, and TES capacity. Moreover, the infeasible optimization can cause a significant income loss, which can be up to 12.5% of the daily profit. Therefore, incorporating SOC-dependent TES constraints is essential for generating operationally feasible and economically accurate dispatch schedules, particularly when evaluating multi-market strategies or TES capacity expansion.

title: Comparative thermodynamic and techno-economic analysis of ammonia engine with partial pre-cracking versus natural gas engine with carbon capture and storage: towards well-to-wake maritime decarbonization
Inter-annual electricity balancing in 100% renewable energy systems assessed through a techno-economic comparison of data series length, e-hydrogen versus e-methane, and multi-objective solutions
abstract: Ensuring year-round reliability in isolated 100% renewable energy systems necessitates a strategic combination of generation overcapacity and inter-annual storage, but its optimal design is challenged by uncertainties in weather data and technology choice. This study performs a comprehensive global techno-economic analysis comparing electricity-based hydrogen and electricity-based methane as storage energy carriers across 22-year and 85-year weather datasets. Results reveal electricity-based methane as the superior economic choice for inter-annual electricity balancing, with a global demand-weighted annualised inter-annual balancing system cost approximately 74% lower than for electricity-based hydrogen, driven by significantly cheaper underground storage. Furthermore, this research quantifies the critical risk of under-planning. In the curtailment-optimised case, using 85 weather years increases the required variable renewable energy overcapacity by approximately 57% and storage volume by about 58%, leading to a cost markup increase of roughly 58-59% on a global demand-weighted average compared to the shorter dataset. The cost-optimised case requires the demand-weighted average overcapacity to increase from 5.2% to 8.1%, and the total annualised cost markup of the balancing system to increase from 2.9% to 4.5%. To translate these findings into actionable policy, this work introduces the ‘tau-analogy’, a novel heuristic that systematically identifies balanced and cost-effective solutions on the Pareto front of trade-offs between system cost and inter-annual storage sizing. This research provides strong evidence regarding the hydrogen versus methane debate for inter-annual storage and establishes a new benchmark for data robustness in energy system planning, offering a pragmatic framework for designing economically viable and physically resilient future energy systems.

title: Dynamic operation and thermoneutral load-following control of a pilot-scale solid-oxide electrolysis stack for flexible hydrogen production
abstract: Renewable hydrogen from solid-oxide electrolysis (SOE) is expected to play an important role in decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors and linking variable renewable electricity with hydrogen production. For industrial deployment, however, SOE systems must operate flexibly under fluctuating electricity supply, and their response to dynamic operation remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigates the thermal response and apparent degradation behavior of a state-of-the-art 75-cell Topsoe SOE stack during a pressurized pilot-scale campaign comprising galvanostatic baseline operation, two load-cycling schemes lasting 48 h and 6 h, and a 72-h load-following experiment using a self-regulating thermoneutral control strategy. Baseline operation at -0.62 A/cm 2 before and after load-cycling yielded voltage degradation rates of 25.8 mV/kg H 2 and 10.4 mV/kg H 2 , respectively, while the corresponding area-specific resistance degradation rates were 16.5 mΩ⋅cm 2 /kg H 2 and 19.2 mΩ⋅cm 2 /kg H 2 . Because these changes may also reflect continued early-life stack conditioning or reversible recovery phenomena, they cannot be directly attributed to load-cycling, and no measurable degradation penalty was identified under the tested conditions. Thermal analysis showed that the transition from open-circuit voltage to electrolysis operation was the most severe transient during load-cycling, with a maximum inlet-to-outlet gas temperature difference of 11.1 °C. During the 72-h load-following experiment, the thermoneutral control strategy maintained this temperature difference within ±3 °C while operating between -0.47 A/cm 2 and -0.62 A/cm 2 , corresponding to 75-100 % of nominal load. The results demonstrate that thermoneutral load-following operation is achievable in the tested pilot configuration. However, dedicated long-term degradation studies remain necessary to assess whether this operating strategy is compatible with durable performance under application-relevant dynamic conditions.

title: Cross-domain photovoltaic cell fault diagnosis using electroluminescence images
Integration of high-temperature heat pump and thermal energy storage for enhancing energy flexibility in eco-industrial clusters
abstract: This study presents a techno-economic framework for integrating high-temperature heat pumps (HTHP) with thermal energy storage (TES) systems to optimize industrial waste heat recovery within eco-industrial clusters. GreenLab, an eco-industrial cluster in Denmark, was chosen as the case study. The framework evaluates system configurations combining renewable wind power, variable waste heat sources, HTHP, and TES. The models incorporate thermodynamic and economic modeling using Aspen HYSYS, structural design of packed-bed TES, realistic cost of materials, and existing models to estimate both capital and operational expenditures. Multiple refrigerants with low global warming potential and zero ozone depletion potential are evaluated. The system performance of three operational scenarios, (a) full-capacity HP-TES, (b) part-load HP with TES, and (c) TES-only, is investigated. The results show that increasing wind power availability significantly reduces the levelized cost of heat. The case of full integration of HP and TES minimizes both the levelized cost of heat and the system downtime. The findings provide insights into the behavior of HP-TES integration in a complex energy system. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive tool for energy system optimization in industrial clusters.

title: A multi-scale framework for the design and deployment of reversible solid oxide cells in photovoltaic-based energy systems
abstract: Reversible solid oxide cell (rSOC) systems are a promising bidirectional conversion technology for bridging the temporal mismatch between photovoltaic (PV) generation and demand, enabling long-duration hydrogen storage, combined heat and power, and sector coupling. Existing rSOC studies, however, treat stack-level electrochemical performance and system-level deployment largely in isolation, so stack design choices are rarely traced through to energy-system outcomes. This paper develops a multi-scale framework that couples a zero-dimensional electrochemical rSOC model with whole-system mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) optimization. Stack-level sweeps across 650–800 °C, 1–10 bar, and 2,500–10,000 A/m² map a design space in which electrical round-trip efficiency spans ~35–90 % and the active area required per installed kW spans ~0.07–0.40 m², revealing a clear performance–size trade-off. Then, part-load characterization is performed for two selected designs and embedded in the MILP framework through affine inverse-efficiency maps calibrated at minimum- and full-load operation. A capacity–cost sweep (0–16 MW, 500–7,000 EUR/kW) applied to a university campus under three flexibility portfolios shows that rSOC value is strongly context-dependent. Without additional PV systems, operational benefit is limited. With PV system expansion, annualized system cost falls by more than ~30 % at mid-range capacities and self-sufficiency approaches ~95 %, accompanied by substantial CO₂ reductions. When batteries are also available, the economically attractive rSOC window shifts to smaller capacities and lower cost thresholds, indicating a complementary long-duration-balancing role. Robust rSOC deployment decisions thus require co-analysis of stack design, part-load behavior, and flexibility-portfolio interactions.

title: Machine learning framework for integrated catalyst-process modelling for direct conversion of CO2 to dimethyl ether
Synergistic enhancement and flow-thermal interaction of jet-fin hybrid microchannel heat sinks for multi-source non-uniform heat loads
Passive cooling of outdoor LED lights via radiative and non-radiative synergistic processes
Resource-environment-economics coupled assessment for photovoltaic module recycling
Unleashing MIL-53(Al)-(NH2)@Fe2O3 nanocatalyst for biodiesel production from Iranian wild oak (Quercus brantii Lindl) oil: techno-economic assessment and green chemistry metrics
Study on thermal responses of fatty acid/expanded graphite/diatomite shape-stabilized composite phase change materials for buildings
Comparative techno-economic and land-use assessment of photocatalytic water splitting and PV–electrolysis systems for solar hydrogen production
Comparison and analysis of various numerical and machine learning methods for prediction of thermal management system performance and design
Dynamic EIS of fuel cells under transient operating conditions for fault detection
abstract: This study investigates the impedance behavior of fuel cells under varying current conditions, with the aim of developing and evaluating a dynamic EIS-based fault detection methodology. Stationary Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy measurements were first carried out under controlled conditions to characterize the dependence of impedance on current. Based on Equivalent Circuit Models and polynomial approximations, an experimental current-dependent impedance model was established to assess the validity of impedance measurements under dynamic operating conditions. To compute impedance in this non-stationary regime, a dedicated signal processing algorithm was developed. The algorithm compensates for drift effects induced by non-stationarity and enables impedance estimation over short time windows, without requiring the control system to be held at a stationary operating point. Finally, representative driving cycles were applied to identify impedance spectra under dynamic conditions using the proposed model. The results are promising and confirm the relevance of the developed approach.

title: Performance of a novel integrated system combining dual-channel Trombe wall with compression refrigeration for prefabricated cabins in PV power stations
A 20 kW solid oxide electrolysis cell system with hydrogen recirculation: operational performance and thermodynamic evaluation
abstract: To support the growing industrial emphasis on performance of Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cell (SOEC) systems for commercialization, the Korea Institute of Machinery and Materials (KIMM) developed a 20 kW-SOEC system with hydrogen recirculation and conducted a comprehensive thermodynamic assessment of the validated operational performance data. The results demonstrate stable operation for over 3,000 h, with the stack temperature maintained between 730–750 oC and a steam conversion ratio of 32–35%. The overall system electrical efficiency remained above 80% (41.4 kWh/kgH2), whereas the SOEC stacks themselves consumed 35.92 kWh/kgH2. To provide deeper insight into system performance, comprehensive energy and exergy analyses were performed to quantify heat losses and assess thermodynamic irreversibility during the two experiment stages. The energy analysis revealed substantial thermal losses, primarily due to unrecovered latent heat from gas cooling, followed by losses from the stack hot box. In Stage II of the experiment, the thermal insulation of the hot boxes was improved, resulting in a 5.86% reduction in total heat loss and a 1.42% increase in overall system efficiency. The exergy analysis indicated that thermodynamic irreversibility primarily occurred in the SOEC stacks and furnace heaters, accounting for 39.47% and 38.62%, respectively, of the total system exergy destruction in Stage II. The overall system exergy efficiency increased from 76.67% in Stage I to 78.03% in Stage II, confirming that reduced heat losses from the hot boxes contribute to improved system performance.

title: Thermo-electrical performance enhancement of high-concentration photovoltaic systems via multi-parameter optimization of cavity-enhanced heat sinks
Toward cost-competitive sustainable aviation fuel from food waste: process design for CO2 utilization via biogas dry reforming
An active pre-chamber-assisted in-cylinder reforming concept for hydrogen production in single-fuel ammonia engines
Overall cooling performance of a densely packed multirow-hole-array plate for afterburner heat shields under coupled conduction–convection–radiation heat transfer
From biorefinery synergies to sustainable aviation fuel: A critical review of twenty years of renewable fuel pathway evolution
abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production must scale by two orders of magnitude to meet legally binding mandates such as ReFuelEU Aviation and CORSIA, yet the optimal combination of production pathways remains contested. In 2006–2007, Corma, Huber and co-workers proposed that existing petroleum refinery infrastructure could serve as the primary platform for renewable fuel production, a thesis that shaped a generation of research. This critical review traces the evolution of seven SAF-relevant pathways over 2006–2026 and evaluates them against five criteria, feedstock simplicity, infrastructure compatibility, product slate alignment, regulatory qualification timing, and scale economics, through a structured technology scorecard complemented by a parametric levelised cost analysis, drawing on 81 peer-reviewed and institutional sources. Hydrotreating of triglycerides (HVO/HEFA) validated the refinery integration thesis and currently constitutes the largest share of global SAF output, but faces a structural feedstock ceiling of approximately 30–40 Mt/year of available lipids. FCC co-processing has seen limited uptake owing to coking penalties and product slate mismatch with jet fuel specifications. The two fastest-growing pathways, alcohol-to-jet and power-to-liquid, emerged outside the original refinery-centric paradigm. Sensitivity analysis shows that HEFA remains the lowest-cost route below a used cooking oil (UCO) price of approximately 1,028 €/t, beyond which AtJ becomes competitive, while PtL requires regulatory andates rather than cost competitiveness for deployment. Meeting projected SAF demand requires a regionally optimised portfolio of complementary pathways rather than convergence on a single technology, with the refinery repositioned around SAF as its primary product. Global SAF production reached approximately 1.9 Mt in 2025, roughly double the 2024 volume but still less than 1% of total jet fuel consumption. This production level illustrates the scale of the challenge ahead.

title: Thermal-Mechanical fatigue and creep damage characteristics of an efficient and responsive supercritical CO2 cooling wall
Energy, exergy, economic and environmental (4E) analyses of hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron systems with three types of fuel for direct heating
Model-based optimisation of a reversible heat pump-Organic Rankine cycle Carnot battery for residential applications
abstract: Reversible Carnot Batteries are emerging as alternative solutions for renewable energy storage, thanks to their scalability, high energy density, and suitability for seasonal energy storage. Such systems are becoming increasingly competitive for daily energy storage compared to conventional lithium-ion batteries due to their capability to be integrated into multi-energy systems and their lower environmental impact over the entire life cycle. Reversible Carnot Batteries (R-CBs), based on the integration of Heat Pump (HP) and Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC)-based units allows to further reduce the investment costs as the same components are shared. Nevertheless, there is a notable lack of plant analysis of this system when applied on a domestic scale, as well as an assessment of the energy autonomy of the integrated photovoltaic (PV) and R-CB storage system. Indeed, while the literature is rich in thermodynamic and economic analyses, it lacks comprehensive models that consider plant features such as the metallic mass of heat exchangers, piping layout, expander permeability, and mass charge of the working fluid. To fill this gap, a thermo-fluid dynamical model of a reversible Heat Pump–Organic Rankine Cycle (HP–ORC) Carnot Battery for residential applications has been developed and optimized under photovoltaic (PV)-driven operating conditions. The model combines zero-dimensional and one-dimensional approaches to accurately capture both thermodynamic performance and system-level dynamics, including heat exchanger thermal inertia, piping layout, and working fluid mass distribution. Validation against experimental data shows good agreement, with relative errors in the range of 3–6 %. The system is analyzed under winter conditions in central Italy, considering a 60 m 2 PV installation. Results indicate that a thermal energy storage (TES) volume of 8000 L ensures the best trade-off between storage temperature (up to 100 °C) and thermal inertia, in line with those currently adopted in similar applications found in the literature. During discharge, increasing the hot water flow rate from 20 to 30 L·min⁻ 1 results in the power production of a 3 kW ORC unit growing, thus storing up to 4 kWh of electric energy. This ensures that all daily load requirements are fulfilled, with a residual amount of about 1.3 kWh. Another novel aspect highlighted by this work is the assessment of the impact of expander speed on system energy performance. It was observed that reducing the expander speed from 1900 RPM to 1000 RPM increases operating time and improves energy utilization, enabling full load coverage with residual stored energy of 1.5 kWh and peak ORC efficiency close to 7 %. Moreover, the Round-Trip Efficiency (RTE) and exergy efficiency increase by a factor of 2 (34 % and 26 %, respectively) compared to the baseline condition. Therefore, these results open the way for a reversible application of the ORC-based unit as a heat pump to store thermal energy during periods of low electrical energy demand, serving as an alternative to electrochemical storage within batteries.

A multi-scale fusion health indicator and grey transfer framework for PEMFC remaining useful life prediction under cross-condition dynamic profiles
Weather-adaptive reinforcement learning framework for heat pump control under time-of-use tariffs
abstract: Controllers for heat pumps (HPs) in space heating are essential to reduce electricity costs while maintaining thermal comfort for customers billed under time-of-use (TOU) pricing, enabling HPs to act as flexible loads in demand-side management. Although reinforcement learning (RL) can learn cost-optimal control policies, its performance often degrades across outdoor temperatures. To address this limitation, we propose a mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework that trains advantage actor-critic (A2C) RL agents on representative temperature profiles and selects the appropriate agent using temperature forecasts. The proposed framework consistently reduces electricity costs across outdoor temperatures from 10 to −18 °C, achieving an average reduction of 16.5% relative to a well-tuned rule-based controller (RBC) under cold test scenarios, compared to 10.1% for the best single-policy A2C, while also demonstrating greater stability across random seeds. Under colder conditions, the proposed A2C MoE achieves cost reductions of 21.3% and 22.4% relative to the RBC across two datasets, while single-agent A2C baselines show inconsistent performance and may underperform the RBC. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves both cost reduction and generalization to colder outdoor temperatures.

title: A probabilistic assessment of wind ramp behavior and operational risk in the Brazilian Interconnected Power System

Analysis and comparison of the impact of hybrid and wet cooling tower performance on the efficiency of an ammonia–water combined system incorporating a power generation cycle and an absorption refrigeration cycle for subzero applications under various climatic conditions
Firm PV generation through optimized trading and forecasting: Economic and system flexibility impacts
abstract: The growing penetration of variable renewable energy increases the need for strategies that reduce solar-induced flexibility requirements with reliable photovoltaic supply. This study investigates cost-effective trading strategies for utility-scale photovoltaic/smart inverter/battery systems (flexible PV plants) to deliver firm and predictable power to the day-ahead electricity market. An important novelty is the introduction of dedicated key performance indicators for assessing solar supply quality: certainty of supply, supply variability and solar-induced flexibility required from the power system. These metrics are used to compare annual and monthly baseload commitments, forecast-corrected/optimized offers against unconstrained PV supply. Results show that while the provision of a PV baseload 24/365 with 99 % of certainty of supply shows near zero variability and solar-induced flexibility, the minimum production cost is 320 €/MWh firming just 30 % of the unconstrained PV generation. In contrast, forecast-based strategies provide near-firm solar power at costs of 128 and 149 €/MWh while firming 62–72 % of solar generation still ensuring a high supply certainty and low system flexibility requirements. An additional strategy, based on the trading of not only firm output but also the residual variable component (generation splitting), further improves economic performance bringing total production costs closer to market parity while having solar-induced reserves.

title: Dynamic experimental investigation of a liquid air energy storage system assisted by an external cryogenic cold source: Start-up, oxygen redistribution and cyclic stabilization
Thermal design-based waste heat utilization strategies for liquid-cooled data centers in third-generation district heating networks
4E analysis of an integrated ATR-SOEC hydrogen co-production system for deep decarbonization: Energy, exergy, economic, and environmental impacts
abstract: Achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 necessitates the continuous reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions. Conventional hydrogen (H2) production processes, such as steam methane reforming (SMR) and autothermal reforming (ATR), are known to generate relatively high levels of CO2 emissions. In this study, an integrated ATR-Solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) process is proposed to address the dual challenges of achieving future CO2 reduction targets and meeting the increasing hydrogen demand. A techno-economic and environmental analysis is performed. The energy and exergy efficiencies of the proposed hybrid ATR–SOEC process (HASP) increased by 15.0% and 67.0%, respectively, compared with the base process (BAHP). These increases can be attributed to the integration of heat and the additional installation of SOEC. Furthermore, a 12.4% decrease in levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) emissions and a 49.7% decrease in CO2 emissions were observed. The LCOH was calculated and comparatively analyzed by considering carbon taxes by country, electricity costs, and power sources. Additionally, the procurement expenses of natural gas and electricity were identified as the primary cost drivers influencing economic performance in uncertain conditions. The findings of this study may contribute to the development of a sustainable solution for reducing future CO2 emissions, based on conventional H2 production processes.

title: Power and wake of a floating wind turbine in surge motion: Theoretical and experimental investigations
abstract: The deployment of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) necessitates a thorough understanding of how platform motions influence turbine performance under atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) conditions. This study investigates the impact of surge motion on the power and wake characteristics of a model FOWT through integrated theoretical analyses and wind tunnel experiments in simulated ABL flow. Theoretically, we trace the effects from the blade element to the full rotor, developing a first-order analytical framework to interpret surge-induced aerodynamic responses and wake pulsations. Experimentally, we impose mild surge motions (Strouhal number S t = 0 –0.27) on a FOWT model in ABL flow and measure power output and wake velocity. For the mild prescribed surge conditions investigated, results show that surge motion directly induces periodic power fluctuations, with spectral peaks matching the surge frequency. Although the mean power remains largely unaffected, power fluctuations (RMS) increase by up to 230% relative to the fixed-bottom reference case. In the near wake, turbulence intensity increases by up to 200% near the wake centerline, whereas the far-wake mean velocity deficit changes by less than 5% at seven rotor diameters downstream. Surge motion also moderately modulates lateral wake meandering. Spectral analyses of the free-rotation response identify signatures of surge perturbations and turbulent fluctuations. The results indicate that the mean wake properties remain similar to those of a fixed-bottom turbine, supporting the applicability of existing fixed-bottom wake models within the investigated operating regime despite the notable effects on power fluctuations and near-wake turbulence.

title: An exploration of transition pathways for South Africa’s coal-to-liquids complex under long-term national greenhouse gas emissions constraints
abstract: Coal-based industries represent a critical challenge for long-term energy transitions: their strong economic and energy-security benefits come with the disadvantage of high greenhouse-gas (GHG) emissions. South Africa’s Coal-to-Liquids (CtL) complex in Secunda, which is responsible for around 12 % of national GHG emissions, illustrates these tensions, where rapid or unplanned shutdown could impose substantial economic and energy-security risks. This study evaluates alternative decarbonisation strategies and transition pathways for this CtL complex using an enhanced version of the South African TIMES national energy-system optimisation model. Three pathways are examined: a Baseline case; a Roadmap-Aligned pathway reflecting near-term efficiency with renewable energy integration measures; and a Structural Decarbonisation pathway in which low-carbon technologies are deployed under a national long-term emissions constraint (LTEC). The Roadmap-Aligned scenario reduces facility-level emissions by ∼ 26 % by 2030, decreasing carbon intensity from 0.18 to 0.15 Mt CO 2 PJ −1 . Structural Decarbonisation under a national Long-Term Emissions Constraint of 8.5 Gt achieves deeper cuts of 45 % by 2030, 56 % by 2040 and 62 % by 2045, ultimately lowering carbon intensity to 0.097 Mt CO 2 PJ −1 . While a structural transition is feasible, decarbonisation remains partial. Demand-side electrification, especially uptake of electric vehicles, ease fuel demand and CO 2 constraints, while transition timing is primarily governed by costs of renewable energy and policy ambition, with oil-price dynamics playing a secondary role. Lower oil prices narrow profit margins and reduce Fischer–Tropsch output and Scope 1 emissions, yet result in earlier hydrogen deployment, whilst higher oil prices have the opposite effect. The findings provide strategic insights for policymakers and planners designing industrial transition pathways in carbon-intensive economies.

title: Wiebe combustion modeling of lean ammonia/methane fuel with turbulent jet ignition system
Machine learning-guided design of ORC working fluids for waste heat recovery
abstract: Identifying sustainable working fluid alternatives without compromising system performance is critical for advancing the deployment of Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) technology in renewable energy systems. This study presents a novel computer-aided molecular and process design (CAMPD) methodology developed to design next-generation working fluids for geothermal waste heat recovery in Rankine cycles with different process configurations. The methodology simplifies the complex problem of co-optimizing fluids and cycles into two distinct steps, allowing for the use of detailed cycles and thermodynamic models while effectively managing computational demands. First, flowsheets and operating conditions are optimized for a selection of established fluids using rigorous thermodynamics. Predictive models are then constructed from the resulting optimization data to correlate molecular structure with cycle performance. In the second step, these models facilitate the screening and design of novel fluids without requiring comprehensive characterization. Additional models are employed to predict safety and environmental impact properties, allowing a final multi-objective optimization that seeks to design fluids that effectively balance cycle’s performance, safety and environmental impact. A case study is performed for dual-pressure organic Rankine cycle (ORC) and organic flash cycle (OFC) configurations. The proposed methodology identifies several promising working fluids, including hydrochlorofluoroolefins (HCFOs), with predicted net power outputs of around 16 MW while satisfying the imposed environmental and safety criteria. These computationally designed molecules provide a basis for future thermophysical characterization and experimental validation.

title: Semi-empirical model for cycling aging of lithium-ion battery with C-rate and temperature
Multi-dimensional evaluation of supercritical water gasification to hydrogen coupled with direct reduction steelmaking system
A physics-aware surrogate model based on a graph neural network for mitigating directional discretization bias in wind farm layout optimization
abstract: Coarse directional discretization is commonly used in wind farm layout optimization to reduce the cost of repeated power evaluations. However, the resulting mean generated power can be biased when rapid changes in wake overlap between sampled wind directions are unresolved. In the present study, a physics-aware surrogate model based on a graph neural network is developed to mitigate directional discretization bias in wind farm layout optimization. The surrogate model predicts the directional correction between the coarse directional evaluation and the fine directional reference using a physics-aware correction model, and the graph neural network estimates layout-dependent correction parameters from turbine positions and turbine-pair relations. The surrogate model is evaluated for two measured wind resource cases using 16 wind directions for the coarse directional discretization and 360 wind directions for the fine directional reference. In the a priori evaluation, the mean absolute error, normalized by the fine-directional mean generated power of the reference checkerboard layout, is below 0.8% for both wind resource cases. In surrogate-assisted layout optimization, the a priori and online surrogate frameworks retain 92.1-94.0% and 78.4-89.7% of the improvement obtained by direct optimization using the fine directional reference, respectively. The computational cost of each surrogate framework is less than 8% of the cost required for direct optimization. The surrogate frameworks therefore provide optimization objectives that are more consistent with the fine directional reference than the objective based on the coarse directional discretization.

title: Multivalent ion-enhanced polyzwitterionic hydrogel-based evaporator for efficient solar interfacial desalination and electricity production
A techno-biological framework for the optimization of utility-scale agrivoltaic systems using spatial yield constraints
abstract: The increasing competition for land between agricultural production and solar energy installation poses a major threat to global food and energy security. Agrivoltaic systems, which combine crop cultivation with photovoltaic arrays, help to alleviate this conflict. However, the diverse designs and complex interactions introduce substantial challenges for optimization. This study introduces a process-based biophysical framework for the optimization of utility-scale agrivoltaic systems under structural and spatial yield constraints. The framework includes fixed-tilt elevated, fixed vertical, and single-axis tracking systems, utilizing both monofacial and bifacial photovoltaic technologies. It integrates the physical layout geometries of photovoltaic arrays with dynamic microclimatic irradiance modeling and non-linear canopy photosynthetic saturation curves to evaluate the theoretical photosynthetic performance bounds and energy production metrics. In addition, a spatial optimization methodology governed by a strict ‘80/90 rule’ is presented. This methodology systematically identifies the maximum allowable array densities while ensuring agronomic performance is maintained. The assessment framework was applied across seven different geographic locations in the Americas and Europe, analyzing eleven unique plant species. Results reveal notable variations in optimal array densities, with capacities ranging from 18 to 88 W per square meter (W p /m 2 ). The proposed configurations can improve land-use efficiency, with land equivalent ratio values ranging from 1.05 to 1.90 as a function of latitude and crop-specific photosynthetic response. The proposed framework provides comprehensive guidelines that must be interpreted as an early-stage theoretical screening tool for comparing agrivoltaic layout performance bounds, rather than as a deployment-ready design or commercial optimization model.

title: Exploring plant-level decarbonization options for coal-dependent economies: A techno-economic framework and insights from Indonesia
abstract: A managed transition for the global coal fleet requires robust decarbonization strategies for existing assets. This study develops a plant-level techno-economic framework to evaluate multiple options, including co-firing, carbon capture, and repowering, and applies it to Indonesia’s fleet of 115 coal-fired power plants. Under current market conditions with regulated electricity tariffs, most decarbonization strategies are not cost-effective compared to continued coal operation. The analysis reveals that no single solution is universally optimal and the viability is plant-specific. Direct biomass co-firing is the most applicable option, profitable for 22% of the fleet capacity (4.1 GW), while capital-intensive repowering is only viable for small, inefficient units. Conversely, deep-decarbonization technologies like CCS remain unviable without a carbon price above 50 USD/tCO 2 . The findings demonstrate that a cost-effective transition requires a differentiated and plant-specific portfolio, which is critical for coal-dependent economies worldwide.

title: An artificial intelligence framework for optimizing biomass-based cogeneration using solid oxide electrolysis, desalination, CO2 capture, and methanation
PHiL evaluation of the steam-Rankine cycle dynamic response during real-time cloud events in a PV-CSP hybrid energy system
Energy-loss decomposition and efficiency optimization of volute splitters in centrifugal pumps via a diagnosis-informed design framework
Evaluating BECCS–Biochar systems as hybrid negative emission technologies through life cycle assessment
abstract: Integrating biochar production (BC) with carbon capture and storage (CCS) offers a hybrid negative-emission pathway that may improve carbon removal relative to standalone biochar systems while preserving the long-term permanence of geological storage. This study evaluates a BC + CCS configuration that combines a 350 kg/h biochar production unit with a 10 MW biomass-fired power plant equipped with post-combustion monoethanolamine capture and geological storage. The novelty of the system lies in co-locating two carbon removal routes within a single facility, enabling the use of pyrolysis volatiles while capturing the resulting CO 2 emissions through CCS. Environmental performance was assessed by life cycle assessment (LCA), while carbon sequestration performance was evaluated using the Climate Effect Value (CEV). Standalone BC, bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS), and BC + CCS were compared on a consistent biomass-input and carbon-capture basis. Sensitivity analyses examined the effects of biomass allocation to pyrolysis and pyrolysis temperature. BC achieved strong short-term climate performance (CEV = 0.97 at 30 years) but declined over longer horizons (CEV = 0.32 at 1000 years), whereas BECCS maintained high long-term performance (CEV = 0.94 at 1000 years). BC + CCS showed intermediate long-term permanence while preserving strong near-term sequestration. Environmental performance was also sensitive to system design: increasing the pyrolysis share enhanced substitution benefits from biochar but reduced electricity substitution, while heat-output BECCS and BC + CCS lowered non-climate impacts at the expense of lower CO 2 mitigation. This study demonstrates that integrating biochar production with CCS can provide a scalable hybrid pathway that balances near-term climate benefits with long-term permanence.

title: Multi-timescale coordination of hydro–wind–PV systems with pumped storage for enhanced operational flexibility
An integrated modelling framework of a two-bladed floating VAWT based on two-way fluid–structure interaction
abstract: Vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWTs) are increasingly regarded as promising alternatives for horizontal-axis configurations in large-scale floating wind systems. However, existing coupled modeling tools for floating VAWTs still present several limitations: simplified aerodynamic formulations, inviscid hydrodynamics, quasi-static mooring representations, and limited consideration of composite blade aeroelasticity, hindering accurate multi-physics prediction. To overcome these shortcomings, a comprehensive aero-hydro-elastic-mooring coupling framework is established in this study. The proposed approach integrates the finite element method (FEM) and the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to resolve fluid–structure interaction considering turbulence, waves, and the integral floating VAWT system. The results show that platform motion intensifies the periodic development of leading-edge vortices and dynamic stall by altering the blade relative inflow velocity and effective angle of attack. Although this aggravates the fluctuations of instantaneous torque and power output, it also provides a positive compensating effect on the overall aerodynamic work, resulting in an approximately 6.46 % increase in the mean power coefficient of the floating configuration compared with bottom-fixed one. These platform-motion-induced wake deflection and enhanced turbulent mixing also accelerate recovery, potentially improving array efficiency. Furthermore, the coupled dynamic analysis investigates the nonlinear stress concentrations near the blade-strut, strut-tower, and platform main-column regions, and further reveals the bending-torsional coupled deformation characteristics of the flexible blades. Meanwhile, the mooring system undergoes periodic contact and separation from the seabed, which may induce local scour and fatigue accumulation. Overall, the proposed CFD-FEM framework provides a robust tool for aero-hydro-elastic performance evaluation and structural safety assessment of floating VAWTs, offering valuable guidance for aerodynamic design, integrated load management, and cost-effective offshore deployment.

title: The new generation of piston bowl geometry: a redefinition of paradigms in high-efficiency methane heavy-duty engine design
Prioritizing hydrogen deployment across hard-to-electrify sectors based on system-level environmental performance
abstract: Hydrogen is widely considered as a key option for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors; however, identifying where and how it should be deployed requires system-level, multi-impact assessment to avoid environmental burden shifting. This study aims to determine environmentally optimal hydrogen deployment pathways and sectoral priorities for Finland’s energy transition using a scenario-based, system-level LCA. The analysis integrates multiple hydrogen production pathways and their conversion into hydrogen-derived fuels and chemicals, which are deployed across steel, shipping, aviation, heavy-duty transport, chemical production, and oil refining sectors under alternative transition scenarios. Environmental performance is evaluated across five midpoint impact categories: climate change, acidification, fine particulate matter formation, marine eutrophication, and ozone depletion, calculated by using the ReCiPe method. Results show that 100 % wind-powered electrolysis-based hydrogen delivers the highest overall environmental performance, reducing national climate change impacts by 80 % (from 30.8 to 6.2 Mt CO 2 ,eq./a) and decreasing other environmental impacts by 47–76 %. Beyond conventional LCA results, this study introduces two novel deployment priority indices (DPIs) to translate multi-impact outcomes into decision-relevant guidance. The system-weighted DPI identifies sectors where hydrogen deployment yields the greatest reduction in national environmental impacts, while the sector-intrinsic DPI ranks transitions based on their internal multi-impact environmental efficiency, independent of sector size. By jointly applying these two DPIs within a unified system-level LCA framework, this study provides a novel, transparent basis for prioritizing hydrogen deployment across sectors, enabling strategic, impact-driven decision-making and efficient allocation of renewable energy resources.

title: Multi-objective optimisation of renewable energy integration in circular brine valorisation/treatment: The case of the CARMEn chain
abstract: Circular brine-valorisation chains offer a promising route to address water scarcity and critical raw-material recovery, but their large electrical and thermal energy demands can offset environmental benefits if powered by fossil sources. This work develops a fully integrated, hourly resolved simulation and multi-objective optimisation framework for the CARMEn treatment chain − combining nanofiltration, Mg(OH) 2 precipitation, softening, electrodialysis with bipolar membranes, membrane distillation and reverse electrodialysis – coupled with a hybrid solar energy system comprising photovoltaic panels, lithium-ion battery storage, flat-plate solar-thermal collectors and a hot-water storage tank. Three representative brine feeds are analysed at a saltwork site in Trapani (Italy): reverse-osmosis brine, nanofiltration retentate and saltwork bittern, each targeting 50 t/y of Mg(OH) 2 production. A deterministic Python model computes 8760 h energy balances, system dispatch, discounted cash flows and operational CO 2 emissions. A multi-objective genetic optimisation algorithm explores the trade-offs between net present value, electrical and thermal coverage, and capital expenditure. Results show that all scenarios are economically viable at baseline market conditions (net present value of 224–277 k€, internal rate of return of 11–11.5 %, payback of about 8 years), with nanofiltration retentate achieving the best economic performance. Bittern attains comparable renewable shares (electrical coverage of 54 %, thermal coverage of 74 %) at the lowest capital expenditure (514 k€). Sensitivity analysis identifies the electricity export tariff as the primary economic driver, while battery capital cost governs storage sizing, with an economic break-even threshold around 150 €/kWh. Avoided CO 2 emissions range from 37.8 t/y for bittern to 85.4 t/y for reverse-osmosis brine, with the thermal contribution dominating in heat-intensive scenarios. The proposed framework provides a systematic tool for the co-design of solar-powered circular brine-valorisation systems, with the specific quantitative results reflecting the solar resource and regulatory context of the Trapani case study considered here.

title: Techno-economic and thermodynamic assessment of three Solar-Driven CO2-to-Acetic acid pathways
Dynamic optimisation of a novel integrated CSP-brayton and geothermal battery system
abstract: Existing CSP--geothermal hybrid systems treat the subsurface reservoir as a fixed-temperature heat source. How waste heat from a solar-driven power cycle can progressively upgrade reservoir temperature, and how such a system should be operated transiently under realistic solar forcing, has not been examined. A supercritical CO₂ regenerative Brayton topping cycle is coupled with a double-flash geothermal bottoming cycle through a novel underground thermal energy storage mechanism, termed the geothermal battery, in which waste heat rejected from the Brayton cooler is continuously injected into the subsurface to upgrade the reservoir at the near-field extraction well. A four-mode thermal arbitrage dispatch framework governs hourly heat allocation between surface thermal energy storage and the subsurface reservoir. The integrated system is assessed over a 25-year transient simulation driven by real direct normal irradiance data at the Ulumbu geothermal field, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. Bayesian optimisation over a ten-dimensional design space, subject to a high-side pressure constraint of 30 MPa, reveals an intrinsic conflict between maximising net electrical output and maximising reservoir charging temperature. The Pareto knee-point balances these objectives at a 25-year cumulative net electrical output of 8,737 GWhe and a cumulative geothermal heat gain of 22,652 GWhth, corresponding to a quasi-steady system net power of 47.9 MWe. Thermal breakthrough at the production well occurs within approximately 0.7 years, after which the produced temperature stabilises over 300°C. The geothermal battery delivers a sustained gain of +34 MWth in geothermal heat input, +8 MWe in bottoming-cycle net power, and approximately 2 percentage points in overall system efficiency relative to operation without subsurface heat accumulation. These gains plateau by year 1.5--2.0 and are maintained indefinitely, establishing the geothermal battery as a one-time thermal investment with a continuous return.

title: Optimal waste heat temperature in semiconductor cleanroom HVAC: Configuration-dependent cost structure and operating strategy
abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems account for a large share of the energy use of advanced semiconductor fabrication facilities (fabs). Recovering chiller condenser waste heat to outdoor air conditioner (OAC) heating coils in place of LNG boiler heating has emerged as an efficiency measure. The waste heat temperature is the condenser water return temperature (CWRT), which simultaneously governs chiller coefficient of performance, cooling tower fan power, recoverable heat, and auxiliary boiler use. Prior work, however, remains limited to individual demonstrations, leaving the optimal waste heat temperature across configurations and outdoor conditions unaddressed. This study develops a system simulation of a fab OAC and thermal utility system. It analyzes the cost of displacing LNG heating with waste heat for two configurations differing in backup heating scope: a steam-backup hybrid and a boiler-free variant. The cost divides into a high-gain boiler displacement region, a steam humidification plateau, and a loss region with nothing left to displace. This structure is robust to LNG price variation. Both optima are closely approximated by tracking the lowest CWRT sustaining the displacement. Annual scenarios of different realization levels evaluate its feasibility and operating window: in central Korea, the strategy cuts the operating cost of one recovery chiller and its matched outdoor-air units by up to about 44% with steam backup and about 42% boiler-free against a boiler-only baseline, most of it realizable without added sensors. Finally, the unit analysis extends to the fab level, relating the chiller conversion ratio to total operating cost to guide operation and design.

title: AGRO – Agrivoltaics layout GeneRation with Optimization framework
abstract: The widespread adoption of ground-mounted photovoltaic systems is facing increasing opposition due to conflicts over land use with agriculture. Agrivoltaics (AV) offers a synergistic solution; however, current design methodologies often treat agricultural constraints and panel layouts as static boundaries, resulting in suboptimal trade-offs between PV-energy conversion and the irradiance available to crops. This study addresses this issue by proposing AGRO: a comprehensive optimization framework that combines the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II), the EnergyPlus dynamic simulation engine, and Python algorithms, treating both agricultural and PV layouts as active decision variables rather than fixed boundary conditions. Applied to a representative Mediterranean case study constrained by Italy’s regulatory framework, the co-optimized layouts improve the trade-off between PV energy generation density and cumulative solar irradiance on cultivated soil, with the system adapting its morphological configuration to protect crop irradiance even during critical seasonal periods for PV-energy conversion. The variable-layout strategy proves effective not only in raising ground-level irradiance but, more distinctly, in making it more uniform across the cultivated cells. This work shows that dynamic spatial allocation enables PV systems to fully comply with Italian legislative constraints while enhancing the solar irradiance available to crops.

title: Application of a heat spreader plate and metal foam for battery thermal management in different cases
Techno-economic assessment and GHG emissions assessment of synthetic LNG production via low carbon power-to-gas (PtoG) pathway
Energy transfer mechanisms induced by draft tube vortices in mixed-flow pump-as-turbine systems
Coordinated dispatch of hydrogen-blended integrated electricity-gas system with heterogeneous energy storage
abstract: To address restricted renewable energy accommodation and limited operational flexibility in integrated electricity-gas systems (IEGS), this paper proposes a collaborative optimal dispatch model considering power-to-hydrogen (P2H), dynamic pipeline hydrogen blending, and heterogeneous energy storage. By characterizing gas flow dynamics, the model unifies the operational constraints of electricity-gas-hydrogen multi-energy flows. The sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is employed to solve this complex nonlinear model. Through progressive scenario comparisons, the synergistic mechanisms of hydrogen blending and heterogeneous storage are systematically analyzed. Simulation results demonstrate that under the all-element collaborative scenario, total operational costs, renewable curtailment costs, and carbon emission costs are reduced by 9.28%, 43.8%, and 1.26%, respectively. This verifies the architecture's effectiveness in enhancing system flexibility. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis reveals that system performance is heavily influenced by the hydrogen blending upper limit and hydrogen storage capacity. An optimal configuration range is identified to balance economic and low-carbon objectives. These findings provide a quantitative basis for the optimal planning and operation of hydrogen-blended coupled systems.

title: Model-driven design and experimental validation of composite PCM for high-rate battery thermal management
Coordinated electricity-heating-water dispatch of an integrated energy system with wind power and flexible seawater desalination load
Pilot-scale solar-driven sweeping gas membrane distillation for seawater desalination: Dynamic modeling, 4E optimization, and seasonal performance
Water-energy-carbon-ecosystem services synergistic optimization to enhance the comprehensive benefits of grain sustainable production
abstract: Sustainable agricultural development increasingly emphasizes the synergistic management of water-energy-carbon-ecosystem services. However, existing optimization frameworks for the water-energy-food-carbon nexus lack integration of ecosystem services and simultaneous consideration of algorithm performance, strategy sustainability, and robustness. To fill this gap, this study develops a decision-making framework for sustainable grain production based on the water-energy-carbon-ecosystem services nexus, incorporating NSGA-II, hypervolume indicator, hybrid multi‑criteria decision‑making, and Monte Carlo simulation (MCS). Application in China's major grain-producing areas demonstrates that systematic cropping structure optimization serves as an effective lever to break the low-sustainability lock-in and achieve a multi-win outcome. By implementing structural adjustments to moderately reduce total sown area, decrease maize cultivation and increase potatoes proportion, these strategies maintain system coordination and stable grain output while delivering substantial sustainability gains: cutting grey and blue water footprints by 192-1,444 and 878-8,738 million m3, reducing GHG emissions by 1.42-15.14 Mt CO₂-eq, saving 901-4,507 million MJ of energy, increasing green water occupancy by 1.74%-2.03% and alleviating water stress by 7.2%-26.9%. Moreover, the optimization strategies exhibit high robustness under 10,000 MCS runs (CV < 0.08). The integrated framework proposed circumvents the exclusion of potential optimal solutions and suboptimal results typical of traditional multi-objective methods. It provides a transferable, data-driven decision-support tool for regions worldwide facing complex resource and ecological constraints, contributing to sustainable agricultural transformation and the advancement of multiple SDGs.

title: Thermodynamic and exergy analyses of an ammonia-fueled gas turbine with chemical recuperation under design and off-design conditions
abstract: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free fuel for gas turbines owing to its high hydrogen density, relatively easy storage and transportation, and compatibility with future zero-carbon energy systems. Ammonia-cracking chemical recuperation has been proposed to improve fuel reactivity and recover gas-turbine exhaust heat. However, the coupled effects of gas-turbine cycle parameters and cracking-reactor parameters under design-point and off-design conditions, as well as the exergy-based mechanism of performance improvement, remain insufficiently clarified. This study develops a component-level steady-state model of an ammonia-fueled chemically recuperated gas turbine (NH3-CRGT), in which exhaust heat drives ammonia cracking and upgrades the fuel before combustion. Ammonia cracking is represented by a thermodynamic-equilibrium model based on Gibbs free-energy minimization. The results show that, at the design point, the NH3-CRGT achieves a thermal efficiency of 36.37%, which is 6.16 percentage points higher than that of the simple-cycle ammonia gas turbine (NH3-SGT). The NH3-CRGT and NH3-SGT show similar design-point parameter selection trends, with an optimum pressure ratio and improved performance at higher combustor outlet temperatures, indicating that ammonia-cracking chemical recuperation can be integrated with an existing SGT platform without fundamentally changing the main-cycle design-point matching. Over the 30%–100% load range, the NH3-CRGT consistently outperforms the NH3-SGT, with thermal-efficiency gains of 3.77–6.16 percentage points and equilibrium cracking conversion above 95%. Exergy analysis shows that the improvement mainly arises from fuel-side chemical exergy upgrading and reduced combustor and exhaust losses. At the rated condition, chemical heat absorption accounts for about 58% of the recovered heat, and the chemical exergy gain accounts for 78.3% of the total fuel-side exergy benefit. These results demonstrate that coupling exhaust-heat recovery with ammonia cracking can improve thermal efficiency, off-design adaptability, and exergy utilization.

title: Optimizing lignin-first biorefinery for sustainable aviation fuel blendstock production: A comparative study of thermochemical and electrochemical hydrodeoxygenation routes
Development and experimental validation of a solar-assisted automated yoghurt manufacturing system: energy, exergy, technoeconomic and product quality assessment
Assessment of hydrogen production potential and energy mismatch reduction of a novel solar-hydrogen cladding system
Technoeconomic assessment of an Allam-cycle-based oxygen storage system under market-driven operation
abstract: This work presents a technoeconomic assessment of an Allam cycle–based energy storage system, evaluated under Spanish electricity market conditions, where oxygen is produced, stored, and later used to decouple power generation from air separation. The analysis compares two configurations, a conventional Allam cycle and an Allam-storage system, benchmarked against a reference Natural Gas Combined Cycle (NGCC). Three natural gas (NG) price scenarios representative of recent Spanish market conditions were examined, and two capital expenditure (CAPEX) levels were considered through a Monte Carlo–based uncertainty analysis. The Allam-storage configuration operates under a peak–off-peak strategy, purchasing low-price electricity for oxygen production and selling power during high-price periods.Across all scenarios, integrating storage consistently improved performance, reducing the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) by up to 12.9% and increasing the Profitability Index (PI) by up to 12.6%. Compared with the NGCC including carbon taxes (65.29 €/tCO2), both Allam-based systems achieved better technoeconomic performance despite 47–77% higher CAPEX, with PI improvements of up to 58%. Optimal storage capacities ranged between 17 and 22 h depending on fuel price. Although still unprofitable under current market conditions, the inclusion of oxygen storage enhances technoeconomic performance and market adaptability, enabling the Allam cycle to exploit price volatility and could contribute effectively to future high-renewable power systems.

title: Thermal radiation and view factor effects on a U-shaped heat pipe heat sink with circular fins under partial vacuum conditions for avionics applications
abstract: This study experimentally investigates the thermal performance of a U-shaped heat pipe heat sink (HPHS) integrated with circular fins for avionics thermal management under partial vacuum conditions. The investigation focuses on the influence of thermal radiation, radiation view factor, apparent natural convection, fin performance, and optimisation of the evaporator-to-condenser length ratio. Experiments were conducted under both partial vacuum and atmospheric conditions with heating powers ranging from 3 to 22 W. Three thermal models were evaluated, including radiation analysis with radiation view factor, radiation analysis without view factor, and convection-only analysis. The results show that the total thermal resistance decreases with increasing heating power due to enhanced phase-change heat transport within the heat pipe. Neglecting the radiation view factor substantially overestimates the radiation heat transfer by approximately 198 %, leading to unrealistic prediction of the radiation-to-convection heat transfer ratio and underestimation of the apparent natural convection coefficient. Despite the reduced-pressure environment, the apparent natural convection remains the dominant heat transfer mechanism throughout the investigated operating range. The fin efficiency and fin effectiveness decrease with increasing heating power, while the optimisation analysis indicates that the optimal evaporator-to-condenser length ratio under partial vacuum conditions remains relatively small, ranging from approximately 0.015 to 0.038, indicating the necessity of a substantially longer condenser section for effective heat dissipation. The findings provide important design guidelines for compact passive cooling systems in avionics and aerospace electronic applications.

title: Location-dependent biofuel process design from an integrated techno-economic and environmental perspective – A Central European case study
abstract: Second generation biofuels from biomass residues constitute an essential alternative for their fossil counterparts to decrease transport’s climate impact.
